decisions.reason: Launched only a year ago with its own web page, the adjustable quarter-pallet display fits the firm's announced point-of-sale display line, so tooling and design costs already sunk and the visible commitment favor persisting.
The pegboard-back shelf display is a recent, publicly presented part of the display range, and any weak early results can still be read as a temporary ramp-up effect.

The standard quarter-pallet shelf display is central to the display portfolio and cheap to keep alongside related variants, so dropping it after one year would contradict the firm's announced direction.
The eighth-pallet display complements the quarter-pallet range the firm committed to publicly, and one year is too short to attribute poor results to anything but temporary causes.
As a wooden product the display pallet is less central to the firm's paper-based core and somewhat more vulnerable, but the recent launch and visible presentation still favor keeping it for now.
The media-product display serves a narrower segment that may disappoint, yet the firm's investment and public presentation make it likely to give the product more time.
